label: hv-morph-fin-locomotion
topic: Fish fin and swimming statements: Strouhal number range, elongated-body theory, fin-ray bilayer bending, glide ratio bounds
summary:
Harvested 10 statements; 7 rest on abstracts or metadata I opened (PubMed, Crossref), 3 are from memory and listed in could_not_find. Three validations ran against reported numbers. (1) The narrow optimal-efficiency Strouhal band 0.25-0.35 FAILS as a description of real swimmers: only 55% of 248 measured cetacean values fall in it, and the mode sits about 20% lower (0.225-0.275). (2) The broad band 0.2-0.4 passes only at species-mean level, with considerable scatter. (3) Flying-fish glide: steady-glide ceiling h*(L/D) = 13.2 m * 4.7 = 62 m against a simulated 45.4 m, a pass, but a weak one because both numbers come from the same CFD paper. A derived point: the two reported kinematic windows (amplitude/length 0.15-0.25, normalised frequency 1-2) only force St into [0.15, 0.5], so the 0.2-0.4 band is extra information, not a consequence of them.

LEAN: NOT PROVED. One file with four theorems (Strouhal factorisation, Strouhal window, Lighthill thrust sign iff wave speed > swim speed, glide range bound) was written at D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/hv-morph-fin-locomotion/FinLocomotion.lean. Both permitted check runs FAILED at line 1 (import Mathlib) with 'failed to read file ... .olean.private', a different Mathlib file each time; the first named file exists on disk, so this looks like an environment or contention fault in the shared Mathlib cache, not a proof error. The proofs themselves were never elaborated, so their correctness is unknown.

Registry overlap (grep only, not read in depth): lift-to-drag is already present (lean/constraints.json lift_to_drag_max; tracks/research/lean/t4-glide-law__MaxLiftToDrag.lean; t4-glide agents). Fin ray appears in tracks/research/agents/pp-fish-biomechanics-morphology.json. Strouhal, elongated-body and Bainbridge terms hit in tracks/research (t4-glide and pp-fish agent files) but I did not confirm any Lean law for Strouhal or Lighthill thrust in lean/ or tracks/lean; treat those as probably new. No file was written to the repo. Based on articles retrieved from PubMed; DOIs are given per finding.

findings.claim: S1 Strouhal band. Formal: St := f*A/U; for cruising lift-based swimmers 0.2 < St < 0.4 (assumption: steady cruise, oscillatory lift-based propulsion). Registry: Strouhal term found in tracks/research agent files, no Lean law confirmed. Falsifier: per-species f, A, U table in Rohr and Fish 2004 (JEB, open); test = fraction of species means outside [0.2,0.4] > 0. VALIDATED: prediction species means in [0.2,0.4]; measured: each species average within range (6 cetacean species, 248 values) -> PASS at mean level, with considerable individual scatter.
findings.evidence_quote: usually peaks within the interval 0.2 < St < 0.4
findings.confidence: high for the statement (abstract opened); validation uses the Rohr and Fish abstract only, not the table

findings.claim: S2 Narrow efficiency optimum. Formal: St in [0.25, 0.35] at maximum propulsive efficiency (oscillating-foil prediction, attributed to Triantafyllou et al. 1993). Registry: not found. Falsifier: same cetacean table; test = share of observations inside [0.25,0.35]. VALIDATED: prediction most values in 0.25-0.35; measured 55% inside, versus 74% in 0.20-0.30 and mode 0.225-0.275 -> FAIL as a tight bound (observed values about 20% lower than predicted).
findings.evidence_quote: between 0.20 and 0.30 (74%) than the 0.25-0.35 (55%) range predicted
findings.confidence: high for the measured shares; the 1993 primary source for the 0.25-0.35 prediction was not opened

findings.claim: S3 Kinematic windows. Formal: k := f*L/U in [1,2] and a := A/L in [0.15,0.25] for toothed cetaceans; then St = a*k (identity) so St in [0.15, 0.5]. This is wider than 0.2-0.4, so the band is not implied by the windows. Registry: not found. Falsifier: same table; test = any animal with k or a outside the window while cruising. Consistency check: midpoint 0.2*1.5 = 0.30, observed mode 0.225-0.275 lies inside [0.15,0.5] -> PASS (weak, necessary only).
findings.confidence: high for the windows; the derived interval is my own arithmetic, Lean proof written but unchecked

findings.claim: S4 Elongated-body theory, wave speed. Formal: for a slender fish with body wave h = g(x - V t), mean thrust T = (m/2)*(V^2 - U^2)*g'^2 at the tail (m = added mass per length), so T > 0 iff V > U; recommended V about (5/4)*U for high Froude efficiency. Assumptions: slender body, inviscid, small amplitude. Registry: 'Lighthill'/'elongated' hits in tracks/research only; no Lean law confirmed. Falsifier: any open kinematics table giving body-wave speed V and swim speed U (for example midline kinematics in Dryad swimming datasets); test = any steady swimmer with U/V >= 1. Not validated against data here.
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022112060001110 (Crossref record opened; abstract seen only as a paraphrase by the fetch tool)
findings.value: V approx 1.25 U; thrust requires V > U
findings.confidence: medium: the 5/4 figure came through a tool paraphrase of the abstract, not a verbatim read; the thrust formula is from my memory of the theory

findings.claim: S5 Fin-ray bilayer stiffness control. Formal: a fin ray is two bending half-rays (hemitrichs) joined along their length; a base offset d between them sets curvature, and effective bending stiffness K(actuated)/K(unactuated) > 10; curvature is concentrated at the base or at the load point. Assumption: linear elasticity. Registry: 'fin ray' appears in tracks/research/agents/pp-fish-biomechanics-morphology.json; no Lean law confirmed. Falsifier: force-displacement curves in the open PMC article (PMC2359861); test = stiffness ratio between actuated and unactuated < 10.
findings.evidence_quote: variation in ray stiffness over more than an order of magnitude
findings.confidence: high for the qualitative bound; exact ratio not read from the full text

findings.claim: S6 Flying-fish glide ratio ceiling. Formal: (L/D)max = 4.7, so minimum steady glide angle = atan(1/4.7) = 12.0 degrees, and steady glide distance x <= h*(L/D)max. Registry: lift_to_drag_max already in lean/constraints.json and tracks/research/lean/t4-glide-law__MaxLiftToDrag.lean (value there not compared). Falsifier: wind-tunnel polar in Park and Choi 2010 (JEB); test = measured L/D max of the fins-spread model exceeds the bound in use. VALIDATED: prediction x <= 13.2 m * 4.7 = 62.0 m; reported glide 45.4 m -> PASS (weak: same CFD paper, and the launch is powered, not a pure steady glide).
findings.evidence_quote: maximum lift-to-drag ratio of 4.7 is achieved
findings.value: L/D max 4.7; CL max 1.03; distance 45.4 m; height 13.2 m
findings.confidence: high for the reported numbers; they are simulation results, not field measurements

findings.claim: S7 Flying-fish polar shape. Formal: argmax over attack angle of L/D is near 0 degrees; argmax of lift coefficient is at 30-35 degrees; L/D rises near the sea surface (ground effect), i.e. L/D(h small) > L/D(h large). Registry: glide content exists in t4-glide agents; these specific angle statements not confirmed there. Falsifier: Park and Choi wind-tunnel tables; test = L/D peak outside about -5..5 degrees, or no L/D gain at small height.
findings.evidence_quote: lift-to-drag ratio was maximum at attack angles of around 0 deg
findings.value: L/D max at about 0 deg; CL max at 30-35 deg
findings.confidence: high for the angles; the abstract gives no L/D number, so I did not quote one

findings.claim: S8 Swimming-number scaling. Formal: with Sw := f*A*L/nu and Re := U*L/nu, Re ~ Sw^(4/3) in the laminar regime and Re ~ Sw in the turbulent regime, which implies St roughly constant (about 0.3) at high Re. Registry: not found. Falsifier: the paper's supplementary table of swimmers (use only non-held-out rows); test = log-log slope of Re on Sw outside 1.0 +/- 0.1 for Re > 1e4.
findings.value: Re ~ Sw^(4/3) laminar; Re ~ Sw turbulent
findings.confidence: low: stated from memory, source not opened this session

findings.claim: S9 Speed proportional to tail-beat frequency. Formal: U/L = (3/4)*(f - 4/3) for f above about 5 Hz, i.e. U = (L/4)*(3f - 4) (dace, trout, goldfish). Registry: 'Bainbridge' hits only in tracks/research agent files. Falsifier: any open f-U-L table for a teleost (for example FishBase swimming-speed table); test = slope of U/L on f differs from 0.75 beyond its confidence interval.
findings.source: Bainbridge 1958, Journal of Experimental Biology 35:109-133 (NOT opened)
findings.confidence: low: from memory, source not opened, coefficients unverified

findings.claim: S10 Optimal Strouhal depends on drag. Formal: the efficiency-optimal St is a function of the drag coefficient and tail aspect, giving a predicted window wider than 0.2-0.4 across animals. Registry: not found. Falsifier: same per-species St tables; test = observed St not ordered by body drag coefficient as predicted.
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfluidstructs.2012.02.008 (Crossref metadata opened; no abstract in the record)
findings.confidence: low: only title, author, journal and pages were confirmed; the numeric window is not quoted because I could not read it

key_claims: The narrow 0.25-0.35 Strouhal optimum fails on real cetacean data: only 55% of 248 values fall inside, and the mode is about 20% lower.
The broad 0.2-0.4 Strouhal band holds for species means but not for individual observations.
Amplitude and frequency windows alone only bound St to [0.15, 0.5]; the 0.2-0.4 band is an independent empirical claim.
Flying-fish L/D max of 4.7 gives a minimum steady glide angle of about 12 degrees and a 62 m ceiling from 13.2 m height; the reported 45.4 m is inside it.
The Lean file was written but NOT checked: both check runs failed reading Mathlib build files, so nothing is proved.
lay_summary: A fish pushes itself forward by wagging its tail, and scientists divide how fast and how wide the tail wags by how fast the fish swims to get one number called the Strouhal number.
Many swimming animals keep that number between about 0.2 and 0.4, but when we checked real dolphin and whale measurements, the tighter 'best' range people predicted only fit about half the time.
For a fish to move forward, the wiggle travelling down its body has to go backward faster than the fish goes forward.
Each fin ray is like two thin strips stuck together; sliding one strip against the other makes the ray bend and can make it more than ten times stiffer.

A flying fish gliding in air travels at most about 4.7 metres forward for each metre it drops, and the numbers we found fit that limit. The computer proof file we wrote could not be checked because the proof library failed to load, so it does not count as proved.

glossary.Strouhal number (St): Tail-beat frequency times tail sweep width, divided by swimming speed. A pure number with no units.
glossary.tail-beat frequency (f): How many full tail wags happen each second.
glossary.amplitude (A): How far the tail tip moves side to side in one wag, peak to peak.
glossary.propulsive (Froude) efficiency: The share of the animal's effort that turns into forward motion instead of wasted water movement.
glossary.elongated-body theory: Lighthill's mathematical model of a long thin fish that works out thrust from how the body wave moves.
glossary.body wave speed (V): How fast the wiggle travels backward along the fish's body.
glossary.added mass: The water that has to be pushed aside and so acts like extra weight on the moving body.
glossary.fin ray: One of the thin bony rods that support a fish's fin.
glossary.hemitrich: One of the two half-rods that together make up a fin ray.
glossary.bilayer: Two layers joined together; sliding or stretching one against the other makes the pair bend.
glossary.bending stiffness: How hard something is to bend.
glossary.lift-to-drag ratio (L/D): Upward force divided by slowing force; in a steady glide it equals metres forward per metre dropped.
glossary.glide ratio: Distance travelled forward divided by height lost; equal to L/D in a steady glide.
glossary.glide angle: The downward slope of a glide path.
glossary.angle of attack: The tilt between the body or wing and the oncoming air.
glossary.lift coefficient (CL): A unitless measure of how much lift a wing shape makes.
glossary.ground effect: Extra lift and less drag when gliding very close to a surface such as the sea.
glossary.Reynolds number (Re): Speed times length divided by the fluid's stickiness; tells whether flow is smooth or turbulent.
glossary.swimming number (Sw): Tail frequency times amplitude times body length, divided by the fluid's stickiness.
glossary.laminar / turbulent: Smooth, orderly flow versus messy, swirling flow.
glossary.CFD: Computational fluid dynamics: simulating air or water flow on a computer.
glossary.Lean / Mathlib: A computer program that checks mathematical proofs, and its library of already-proved maths.
glossary.hypothesis (in a proof): An assumption written down by name so the reader can see exactly what the result depends on.
glossary.falsify: To show a statement is wrong by finding data that contradicts it.
